Sleep in less at weekends (needs a little willpower, costs no money).
After an occasional late night, make up for it by going to bed earlier that evening, not by sleeping until noon the next day (cross-reference to upstream item 2.38).

Get outdoors in daylight more, in addition to a fixed wake time (upstream itself says this is inferred from the authors' model and was not tested). Dropped deliberately and disclosed in Zmiany w adaptacji.

findings.text: Jeśli pozwalają na to obowiązki, wybierz zbliżone pory wstawania
findings.why: The upstream action is a fixed wake time that is the same at weekends, and the weekend sleep-in is the specific behaviour upstream asks the reader to cut. No reader-facing instruction field of the item mentions weekends or 'every day'; the weekend appears only as a removal in Zmiany w adaptacji. The cited NHS page says 'every day', so the item is both narrower and more conditional than its own source. The softening is in the safe direction and is disclosed, so a reader is not endangered, but a reader who reads only W praktyce will not learn which days matter.

findings.text: Nie traktuj regularności jako powodu do celowego niedosypiania.
findings.why: Upstream line 8 carries a second action: after an occasional late night, go to bed earlier that evening and do not sleep until noon. It was dropped, and Zmiany w adaptacji does not list the drop (it lists only the light inference and the weekend order). The cited NHS page also addresses this case ('do not sleep in after a bad night's sleep'). The two sources differ in detail (go to bed earlier vs stick to regular hours), so the item has to choose between them with a stated reason. As it stands, a reader who stayed up late is told nothing about the next morning.

findings.text: przeznacz wystarczająco dużo czasu na sen
findings.why: The upstream action is only a fixed wake time. 'Allot enough time for sleep' (and the title's 'nie skracając odpoczynku') is not in the upstream span, and the NHS snapshot gives only average sleep need and says it varies; it does not advise allotting time. For a reader with insomnia, which is the context of the cited NHS page, the same page advises going to bed only when sleepy, so 'allot time' can be read as more time in bed. The action is wider than the source, is not labelled as an editorial addition, and Zmiany w adaptacji does not mention it.
